title: Qualify network ownership at a remote pumping station
principalTechnique: Timestamped bounded command ownership with local fallback
objective: Calculate the remote-loop delay reserve, reject ineligible command packets, and prove bounded transfer between remote coordination and local pressure control.
physicalPurpose: Keep a distribution header locally controlled when remote command timing, ordering, quality, or clock evidence is no longer trustworthy.

simplifications: Each header is a self-regulating first-order pressure model rather than a full pump curve and pipe network.
The packet record is injected deterministically and does not measure a deployed transport.
The sequence comparison excludes sender restart, session identity, integer wrap, authentication, and malicious traffic.
The linear delay-margin calculation does not prove nonlinear hydraulic or physical-station safety.

baseline.limitation: The receiver applies every arrival and retains it indefinitely, so stale, reordered, poor-quality, and clock-invalid commands can own the pump.

change.decision: Accept remote ownership only while locally calculated age, order, quality, synchronization, uncertainty, range, and recovery conditions all pass; otherwise use the tracked local PI controller.

disturbances: Omit packets until the retained eligible command expires.
Deliver stale, reordered, bad-quality, unsynchronized, excessive-uncertainty, and impossible-future packets.
Restore a newer eligible command through explicit recovery approval at the current applied command.

acceptance.window: each first ineligible scan through local ownership

abortPredicates: A required pressure, time, uncertainty, demand, or command is nonfinite or leaves its declared hard range.
The packet schedule, plant, controller interval, substep, initial state, limits, or evidence class differs without declaration.
An ineligible packet gains protected remote ownership or expiry takes more than one station scan.
Recovery is applied without explicit approval or produces more than 2 percentage points of command discontinuity.
safety.restorationMode: Transfer to the tracked local pressure PI controller; restore remote ownership only with a newer eligible command and explicit approval at a matched command.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised pumping-station controls engineer with network, electrical, hydraulic, operations and safety owners
simulationOnlyRestrictions: No physical pump, drive, valve, pressure system, gateway, or network is operated.
Injected timestamps and packet states are controlled test inputs, not measurements of deployed network performance.
Physical application requires reviewed clock, session, cybersecurity, pump-protection, hydraulic, failover, and approval evidence.

video.viewerOutcome: Explain why a locally calculated bounded communication contract is part of loop stability and safe command ownership.

learning.context: A remote coordinator can request pump speed, but the pumping station owns local pressure measurement, local time, local fallback, and final drive authority.
learning.reason: A controller qualified on a local deterministic path does not remain qualified when transport delay, jitter, loss, order, and clocks become part of its loop.
theory: Packet age is calculated from locally generated time, a source timestamp, and bounded clock uncertainty.
Latency, jitter, loss, reordering, buffering, and synchronization consume different parts of the communication and stability contracts.
A model-based delay margin must exceed a conservative end-to-end delay budget with positive reserve.
The local controller tracks the remote owner so an approved transfer does not create an avoidable actuator step.
learning.workedPrediction: Calculate a 1.984 rad/s gain crossover, approximately 0.855 s delay margin, 0.47 s conservative budget, and approximately 0.385 s reserve before injecting a packet.
practicalPreparation: Verify both equivalent plant copies, the 100 ms task, 20 ms substep, packet record, age/order limits, local fallback, rejection reasons, measures, aborts, and Simulation label.
Record expected ownership and rejection reason for every packet before running.
learning.baseline: Run the arrival-order-only receiver, which applies every delivered command and retains the last arrival indefinitely.
learning.change: Run the timestamped bounded receiver against the same packet record with the tracked local PI fallback enabled.
learning.comparison: Compare invalid ownership, transfer time, approved recovery step, pressure absolute-error area, peak pressure departure, applied-speed travel, and qualified remote availability.
learning.validation: Reproduce all six rejection classes, exact delay calculations, independent packet decisions, paired plant dynamics, bounded outputs, one-scan transfer, and approved recovery.
learning.explanation: Trace each packet field into age, order, rejection, ownership, requested and applied pump speed, then header pressure.
learning.transfer: Carry the bounded communication contract into Lesson 74, where timely packets still cannot prove that multirate sensors and actuators are healthy.
